title: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum. Explain Kadane's algorithm.
shortTitle: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm) — running sum reset at negatives

s1_definition.profdef: Kadane's algorithm scans once, maintaining the best subarray sum ending at the current index as current = max(num, current + num), and the global answer as the max over all current values. Restarting with num alone whenever the running sum would hurt (current + num < num) captures the optimal ending-here sum, so the global maximum emerges in O(n) time and O(1) space.
s1_definition.analogy: Scanning daily net cash flows at National Bank of India, you track the best streak ending today: either extend yesterday's streak by today's amount, or start fresh today if the past streak is dragging you down. The best streak ever seen is your answer.
s1_definition.oneliner: current = max(num, current + num); answer = max(answer, current) — extend or restart each step.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Kadane's algorithm scans once, maintaining the best subarray sum ending at the current index as current = max(num, current + num), and the global answer as the max over all current values. Restarting with num alone whenever the running sum would hurt (current + num < num) captures the optimal ending-here sum, so the global maximum emerges in O(n) time and O(1) space.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Scanning daily net cash flows at National Bank of India, you track the best streak ending today: either extend yesterday's streak by today's amount, or start fresh today if the past streak is dragging you down. The best streak ever seen is your answer.

**One line to remember:** current = max(num, current + num); answer = max(answer, current) — extend or restart each step.

sections.s2_technical:
Initialize both current and answer to the first element. For each subsequent number, set current to the larger of the number alone or current plus the number, then update answer. For example: `current = Math.max(num, current + num); best = Math.max(best, current);`.

Choosing the number alone effectively discards a negative prefix, because any prefix that made the running sum worse than starting fresh can never be part of an optimal subarray ending here. Initializing to the first element (not zero) handles all-negative arrays correctly, returning the largest single element.

The time is O(n) and the space is O(1). A senior nuance is that tracking the start and end indices alongside the sums recovers the actual subarray, and that a divide-and-conquer solution exists in O(n log n) but Kadane's linear scan is strictly better.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, analysts find the most profitable contiguous run of daily net cash flows to identify a peak performance window. This is exactly how Maximum Subarray works.

Problem 2 — A losing stretch at the start of a window should be dropped rather than dragging the total down. This is exactly why the running sum restarts when extending would be worse than starting fresh.

The mini-project builds a `PeakWindowFinder`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input flows are minus two, one, minus three, four, minus one, two, one, minus five, four.

Step 1: current and best both start at minus two; at one, current restarts to one and best becomes one.

Step 2: At minus three, current becomes minus two; at four, current restarts to four and best becomes four.

Step 3: At minus one current is three, at two it is five, at one it is six, so best climbs to six.

Step 4: At minus five current drops to one, at four it becomes five, but best stays six.

Step 5: The peak window sum is six, from the run four, minus one, two, one.

```text
2026-10-27T01:05:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Peak Cash-Flow Window (Kadane)
2026-10-27T01:05:00Z [INFO] Peak contiguous cash-flow window sum = 6
2026-10-27T01:05:00Z [INFO] Best = 6
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Maximum Subarray is solved by Kadane's algorithm in a single linear pass. I keep two values: the best subarray sum ending exactly at the current position, and the best sum seen anywhere so far. At each element I set the ending-here sum to the larger of the element alone or the previous ending-here sum plus the element, which is the decision to either start a fresh subarray or extend the existing one. Then I update the global best.

Restarting with the element alone is what discards a harmful negative prefix, because any prefix that dragged the running sum below starting fresh can never be part of an optimal subarray ending at this position. Initializing both values to the first element, rather than zero, is the detail that makes all-negative arrays return the largest single element correctly.

In my project at National Bank of India, analysts needed the most profitable contiguous run of daily net cash flows to pinpoint a peak performance window, and Kadane's computed it in one pass over the ledger. When the team needed the actual window and not just its total, I tracked the candidate start and end indices alongside the sums to recover the exact span.
